statement: For four general individually F-defined lines in P^3 over a field F of characteristic different from two, the arithmetic count is Σ_L Tr_(F(L)/F)⟨λ_L−μ_L⟩ = ⟨1⟩+⟨−1⟩ in GW(F). Here λ_L is the cross-ratio of the four intersection points on L and μ_L is the cross-ratio of the four planes spanned by L and the input lines, with the same ordering.

source.location: Theorem 1 and its definitions (printed p.2); real-signature consequence on p.3; proof in Section 6

scope: Four ordered, individually F-defined, pairwise skew lines, with the fourth transverse to the quadric ruled by transversals of the first three; char(F)≠2.
notes: The sum is over closed solution lines, using the field trace transfer of quadratic forms. The rank recovers two geometric transversals. Over R the signature is zero, so the two real solutions, when present, carry opposite local signs. The more general Galois-invariant input set in the appendix is not asserted here. The introductory theorem and its definitions were directly inspected; the full proof and appendix were not fully checked.
